title: Federal Reserve Banks: 2024 Report on Payments (2023 Small Business Credit Survey)

history.reason: Source read directly on access date; findings transcribed from the document.

reliability: Primary report by the Federal Reserve Banks on the Small Business Credit Survey. Cover states "Published December 2024"; exact day inferred from the report DOI (sbcs-20241205). Opt-in survey, weighted by the authors.
findings: Fielded September-November 2023; 6,131 responses from small employer firms with 1-499 employees in all 50 states and DC; payments findings use 4,920 firms that answered an optional end-of-survey module (~80% of employer-firm respondents opted in).
About 80% of firms report payments-related challenges; 20% report none.

Payments challenges (N=4,858): fees 52%; customers slow to pay 39%; time-consuming processes such as billing customers and making deposits 20%; delays in settlement or availability of funds 18%; managing multiple payment streams 13%; fraud or theft 11%; customer demand for more options 7%.

Firms collecting payment after delivery, on a schedule, in installments or via a third party more often report slow-paying customers; professional services/real estate and manufacturing are more likely than other industries to take payment after delivery and to report slow payers.
Time-consuming processes and settlement delays are most common among firms paid through a third party.
limitations: Self-reported challenges; no measure of dollar cost, time spent, or willingness to pay.
Optional module: respondents may differ from non-respondents.
Employer firms with 1-499 employees only; excludes non-employer businesses.
Per-industry percentages were shown in a chart that was not cleanly extracted and are not recorded here.
